images.title: Bigger or smaller?
images.purpose: Recap that multiplying by a number less than 1 makes a number smaller, while dividing by it makes the number bigger.
images.composition: One number line across the middle of the frame with a central start point and two curved jump arrows, one jumping left and one jumping right, with a short caption below.
exact_structure: 1 grey #6B7280 number line from 0 to 40, with 5 evenly spaced numbered ticks: 0, 10, 20, 30, 40
1 reddish purple #CC79A7 dot on the tick at 20, the start point, with no extra label (the tick number 20 is enough)
1 teal #0072B2 curved arrow above the line from 20 jumping left to 10, labelled '20 × 0.5 = 10'
1 amber #E69F00 curved arrow above the line from 20 jumping right to 40, labelled '20 ÷ 0.5 = 40'
1 caption line below: 'Using a number less than 1'
rejection: the multiply arrow landing anywhere other than 10, or the divide arrow anywhere other than 40
the arrows pointing the wrong way
images.takeaway: Multiplying by a number less than 1 makes it smaller and dividing by it makes it bigger, so you can order results without computing them.
images.description: A number line from 0 to 40 with a start at 20, a jump left to 10 for 20 × 0.5 and a jump right to 40 for 20 ÷ 0.5.
images.context: Shown beside the pull it together practice on reasoning with decimals.
images.teaching_notes: Use the picture to predict whether each expression is bigger or smaller than its first number before sorting.

image_decisions.why: A compact number line recap of size reasoning supports the ordering and estimating tasks.
